title: New Orleans in the Aftermath of Hurricane Ida

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 每日新闻简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等众多嘉宾。

sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是每日新闻。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: 16 years after Hurricane Katrina, Hurricane Ida was a major test of how prepared cities like New
sentences.zh: 在卡特里娜飓风过去16年后，艾达飓风对新

sentences.en: Orleans now are for extreme weather.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良等城市应对极端天气准备情况进行了重大考验。

sentences.en: Kevin Roos spoke with our colleague, Richard Fawcett, about what worked and what didn't.
sentences.zh: 凯文·鲁斯与我们的同事理查德·福西特谈论了哪些措施有效，哪些无效。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, September 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月2日，星期四。

sentences.en: Richard, hello.
sentences.zh: 理查德，你好。

sentences.en: Hey, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，凯文。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm doing okay.
sentences.zh: 我挺好的。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: I'm here.
sentences.zh: 我在这儿。

sentences.en: Where are you?
sentences.zh: 你在哪儿？

sentences.en: I am in my parents' house in Uptown New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 我在新奥尔良上城我父母的家里。

sentences.en: They've evacuated.
sentences.zh: 他们已经撤离了。

sentences.en: And we're trying to figure out right now whether, like tens of thousands of people, whether it's going to be okay for them to come back.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正试图弄清楚，就像成千上万的人一样，他们回来是不是安全的。

sentences.en: Without electricity, it's just really, really a slog here.
sentences.zh: 没有电，这里简直就是一场漫长而艰难的煎熬。

sentences.en: It looks pretty dark there.
sentences.zh: 那里的光线看起来很暗。

sentences.en: Do you have power?
sentences.zh: 你们有电吗？

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: So how are you?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么样？

sentences.en: You're just talking to us because you have a lot of chargers for your cell phone or something?
sentences.zh: 你跟我们说话是因为你有好几个手机充电器还是怎么的？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, we're running off of batteries and it's just becomes this, you know, just this constant kind of juggling act of running stuff off your car, charging up
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们靠电池供电，这简直就成了一种，你知道的，用汽车供电、给电池充电的不断折腾的过程，

sentences.en: batteries, relying in the Tennessee Williams sense on the kindness of strangers.
sentences.zh: 用田纳西·威廉斯的话来说，就是依赖陌生人的仁慈。

sentences.en: And who are some of the people you've been meeting and talking to?
sentences.zh: 你都遇到了哪些人，跟谁聊过？

sentences.en: Well, after the storm, I kind of set out and visited a few parts of the city to see how people who have a hard time getting by on a sunny day were doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，暴风雨过后，我动身去了城市的几个地方，看看那些在天气好的时候就很难过日子的人过得怎么样。

sentences.en: So one of the places I headed to was New Orleans
sentences.zh: 所以我去的其中一个地方是新奥尔良

sentences.en: East, which is a low-lying, very flood-prone part of the city.
sentences.zh: 东部，那是该市地势低洼、极易发生洪涝的地区。

sentences.en: There is a apartment complex in New
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良

sentences.en: Orleans East called the Willows, which was badly damaged in Hurricane Katrina.
sentences.zh: 东部有一个叫“柳树”的公寓小区，在卡特里娜飓风中损毁严重。

sentences.en: It's been fixed up and a lot of working class people are living there.
sentences.zh: 后来修缮过了，许多工薪阶层的人住在那里。

sentences.en: Hey, what's your name?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你叫什么名字？

sentences.en: My name's Dondrell.
sentences.zh: 我叫东德雷尔。

sentences.en: How do you spell Dondrell?
sentences.zh: 东德雷尔怎么拼？

sentences.en: Including Dondrell Anderson.
sentences.zh: 包括东德雷尔·安德森。

sentences.en: What do you do for a living?
sentences.zh: 你是做什么工作的？

sentences.en: Right now, I'm headed to the barn up the street.
sentences.zh: 现在，我正要去街那头的马厩。

sentences.en: I have two horses up the street.
sentences.zh: 我在街那头有两匹马。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: And I work around the barn.
sentences.zh: 我在马厩周围干活。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: He's a guy in his 30s.
sentences.zh: 他是一个三十多岁的伙计。

sentences.en: He was on a bicycle.
sentences.zh: 他骑着一辆自行车。

sentences.en: His car was in the shop.
sentences.zh: 他的车在修理厂。

sentences.en: And he was, you know, trying to think creatively about how to think his way out of a place that was incredibly hot and incredibly unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 而且他，你知道的，正在发挥创意，想办法离开这个极其炎热、极其难受的地方。

sentences.en: Like right now, I'm currently riding around looking for somebody to help me get in my tires.
sentences.zh: 就像现在，我正四处转悠，找人帮我补轮胎。

sentences.en: I have two snow leaks on.
sentences.zh: 我有两个轮胎慢撒气。

sentences.en: I have a snow leak on two tires.
sentences.zh: 我有两个轮胎都在慢撒气。

sentences.en: On your car?
sentences.zh: 在你的车上？

sentences.en: Yeah, right now.
sentences.zh: 对，就在现在。

sentences.en: So you wanted to get out of town, but you couldn't because you had snow leaks on the tires?
sentences.zh: 所以你想离开小镇，但走不了，因为轮胎慢撒气？

sentences.en: Not only I had snow leaks on the tires, but it's like I know exactly where to go.
sentences.zh: 不仅是轮胎慢撒气，而且就像我知道该去哪里一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, I could have went to Baton Rouge here and here and there, but what I do when I get there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我本来可以去巴吞鲁日这里、那里什么的，但我到了那里能做什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So the problem that Dondrell and many people in the city of New Orleans faces is pretty basic and also pretty tragic.
sentences.zh: 所以，东德雷尔以及新奥尔良市许多人面临的问题非常基本，同时也非常悲惨。

sentences.en: In Dondrell's case, it was a question of having access to a car that could get him out of this kind of this zone of suffering.
sentences.zh: 就东德雷尔而言，问题在于能否弄到一辆车，能带他离开这个苦难的区域。

sentences.en: Do you have money to buy groceries right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在有钱买食品杂货吗？

sentences.en: I promise you, I have a dollar and something sitting in my pocket right now.
sentences.zh: 我向你保证，我口袋里现在就剩一块多钱了。

sentences.en: Mine is probably about a hundred or something out of food stamp, but you can't use that either because there ain't no power, ain't no data.
sentences.zh: 我的食品券大概还剩一百块左右，但你也用不了，因为没有电，没有网络。

sentences.en: I'm just going off, like, you know, my survival skills, you know, that I know, you know, from Katrina and, but I know period.
sentences.zh: 我只能靠，你知道的，我的求生技能，你知道的，从卡特里娜学来的，你知道的，但我懂这些。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Let me ask you right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在问你。

sentences.en: Do you have enough food?
sentences.zh: 你有足够的食物吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to say no.
sentences.zh: 我要说没有。

sentences.en: But yeah, the reason why I say that, because how long is this going to be like this?
sentences.zh: 不过是的，我这么说是因为这种情况还要持续多久？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: So that was the problem for a lot of people in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，这就是许多人面临的问题。

sentences.en: So there he is trying to improvise his way out of something.
sentences.zh: 所以他就这样试图即兴想办法摆脱困境。

sentences.en: OK, OK, we'll go.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧，我们走吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Good luck to you, man.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运，伙计。

sentences.en: It was nice talking to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你聊天。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: There was another woman I met at the apartment complex.
sentences.zh: 我在公寓小区遇到的另一个人。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 嘿，真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: I'm Richard Fawcett.
sentences.zh: 我是理查德·福西特。

sentences.en: I'm from The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: I'm Diane Delpit.
sentences.zh: 我是黛安·德尔皮特。

sentences.en: I'm from New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 我是新奥尔良人。

sentences.en: Her name was Diane Delpit.
sentences.zh: 她叫黛安·德尔皮特。

sentences.en: She's about 40 years old, and she had a very large extended family in the apartment complex.
sentences.zh: 她大约40岁，在公寓小区里有一个很大的大家庭。

sentences.en: I have kids, kids with disabilities.
sentences.zh: 我有孩子，有残疾的孩子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I have three kids with disabilities.
sentences.zh: 我有三个残疾的孩子。

sentences.en: This is my youngest child, Heaven.
sentences.zh: 这是我的小女儿，海本。

sentences.en: She was the face.
sentences.zh: 她就是代表。

sentences.en: You've been here since the hurricane hit.
sentences.zh: 自从飓风袭来，你们就一直在这里。

sentences.en: We went through it.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了这一切。

sentences.en: I have my apartment.
sentences.zh: 我的公寓。

sentences.en: It's been flooded with water.
sentences.zh: 被水淹了。

sentences.en: They had had roof damage, and they're part of the complex.
sentences.zh: 他们的屋顶受损了，他们是小区的一部分。

sentences.en: The water had come through and soaked their wall-to-wall carpeting.
sentences.zh: 水流了进来，浸透了他们满屋的地毯。

sentences.en: We can't live like this.
sentences.zh: 我们不能这样生活。

sentences.en: It's going to kill us.
sentences.zh: 这会害死我们的。

sentences.en: That house can't live in the house.
sentences.zh: 那房子根本没法住人。

sentences.en: No, it's just horrible.
sentences.zh: 不，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: Not with the mold in the...
sentences.zh: 更不用说里面的霉菌……

sentences.en: It's horrible.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: It's like...
sentences.zh: 就像……

sentences.en: Y'all slept in there last night.
sentences.zh: 你们昨晚睡在里面了。

sentences.en: We have, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们睡了。

sentences.en: We slept in there since the hurricane.
sentences.zh: 自从飓风过后我们就一直睡在里面。

sentences.en: It did not seem safe.
sentences.zh: 这看起来很不安全。

sentences.en: We've been without power for three days.
sentences.zh: 我们已经停电三天了。

sentences.en: It's been three days.
sentences.zh: 已经三天了。

sentences.en: I might be exaggerating.
sentences.zh: 我也许有点夸张。

sentences.en: It feel like a lifetime.
sentences.zh: 感觉像过了一辈子。

sentences.en: Yeah, if it's starting to run together for me.
sentences.zh: 对，对我来说时间都有点混淆了。

sentences.en: We don't have no food, no water, nothing cold.
sentences.zh: 我们没有食物，没有水，没有冷饮。

sentences.en: Nobody has came back in and checked on us.
sentences.zh: 没有人回来查看我们的情况。

sentences.en: It's like we just have to survive on our own.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们只能靠自己活下去。

sentences.en: We got to find a way out.
sentences.zh: 我们得找条出路。

sentences.en: We don't have a way out.
sentences.zh: 我们没有出路。

sentences.en: Do you have a car?
sentences.zh: 你有车吗？

sentences.en: No, I don't have a car.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有车。

sentences.en: At the moment, my car is in the shop.
sentences.zh: 目前，我的车在修理厂。

sentences.en: And without electricity, they were forced to kind of make this horrible decision moment after a moment, which is go inside and get out of the heat or go outside and bake in
sentences.zh: 在没有电的情况下，他们被迫一次又一次地做出这种可怕的决定，那就是进去避暑，或者去外面在

sentences.en: the heat and at least get out of the stink of the place.
sentences.zh: 酷暑中暴晒，至少能避开那里的恶臭。

sentences.en: Is your cell phone working?
sentences.zh: 你的手机还能用吗？

sentences.en: My cell phone, I reckon.
sentences.zh: 我想我的手机还能用。

sentences.en: We can't charge our phones.
sentences.zh: 我们没法给手机充电。

sentences.en: We don't have anything.
sentences.zh: 我们什么都没有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The whole family was hoping that some relatives in Baton Rouge could come down and pick them up and take them away.
sentences.zh: 全家人都希望巴吞鲁日的某些亲戚能开车来接他们离开。

sentences.en: But it was kind of tough to be in straight communication with them for all kinds of reasons.
sentences.zh: 但由于各种原因，要与他们保持顺畅的联系相当困难。

sentences.en: The cell service has been very spotty.
sentences.zh: 手机信号一直非常不稳定。

sentences.en: So there was just a lot of confusion about, you know, how they might get away.
sentences.zh: 所以大家对他们究竟该如何离开感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: I'm wishing y'all a whole lot of luck.
sentences.zh: 祝你们好运。

sentences.en: Did I give you my card?
sentences.zh: 我给你我的名片了吗？

sentences.en: No, but please.
sentences.zh: 没有，不过请给我。

sentences.en: When you, uh...
sentences.zh: 当你，呃……

sentences.en: From New York, right?
sentences.zh: 来自纽约，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: When I, when I, uh, when you get the cell service or whatever, I just want to hear it.
sentences.zh: 当、当，嗯，当你恢复了手机信号或者别的什么，我只想听听这个。

sentences.en: Richard, this all sounds really brutal and like there are a lot of people making a lot of very hard decisions.
sentences.zh: 理查德，这听起来真的很残酷，就像有很多人在做出非常艰难的决定。

sentences.en: And I think the obvious comparison to draw is to Hurricane Katrina and to all the horrible images and the footage we all saw of the destruction in New Orleans 16 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为显而易见的对比是卡特里娜飓风，以及16年前我们在新奥尔良看到的灾难的所有那些可怕的画面和录像。

sentences.en: And I know you're from New Orleans and you also covered Hurricane Katrina.
sentences.zh: 我知道你来自新奥尔良，你也报道过卡特里娜飓风。

sentences.en: How would you compare what you've seen over the last few days to what you saw back then?
sentences.zh: 你会如何把你这几天看到的情景和当年看到的进行对比？

sentences.en: Well, Katrina is the, uh, the obvious comparison.
sentences.zh: 嗯，卡特里娜是，嗯，最显而易见的对比。

sentences.en: And it's the, of course, the, the hurricane that, that haunts everyone inside and outside of New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 当然，它也是，嗯，那个让新奥尔良市内外每个人都挥之不去的飓风。

sentences.en: But that's not really what happened here.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是这里实际发生的情况。

sentences.en: You didn't see this massive government breakdown.
sentences.zh: 你没有看到这种大规模的政府瘫痪。

sentences.en: You didn't see this, this massive kind of societal breakdown.
sentences.zh: 你没有看到这种，这种大规模的社会崩溃。

sentences.en: You haven't seen like really kind of horrific confrontations between law enforcement and people trying to get out.
sentences.zh: 你没有看到执法部门与试图离开的人之间那种非常可怕的对峙。

sentences.en: The biggest difference, of course, is that Katrina put 80% of New Orleans underwater and the city struggled mightily to respond.
sentences.zh: 当然，最大的区别在于卡特里娜让新奥尔良百分之八十的面积泡在水里，而这座城市艰难地挣扎着做出回应。

sentences.en: I was driving around an uptown neighborhood after Katrina.
sentences.zh: 卡特里娜过后，我正开车在住宅区上城转悠。

sentences.en: And I remember, you know, in, in this very still moment, um, after the storm, a few days after the storm,
sentences.zh: 我记得，你知道的，在风暴过后那个非常寂静的时刻，嗯，风暴过后几天，

sentences.en: finding an elderly man laid out on his porch with nothing but his name and
sentences.zh: 我发现一位老汉横卧在门廊上，身上除了他的名字和

sentences.en: a social security number, if I recall correctly.
sentences.zh: 一个社会安全号，如果我没记错的话，什么也没有。

sentences.en: And it was just chilling.
sentences.zh: 这简直让人毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: There was no one for me to call.
sentences.zh: 我找不到任何人可以打电话。

sentences.en: Um, there was no one to report it to really.
sentences.zh: 嗯，真的没有可以汇报的人。

sentences.en: Um, this is not exactly that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可不完全是那样。

sentences.en: People aren't finding bodies, uh, in the city.
sentences.zh: 人们并没有在城里发现尸体，嗯。

sentences.en: The physical damage immediately to, to people, uh, and to property is nowhere near the same as it was.
sentences.zh: 对人身和财产造成的直接物理破坏，远不如当年那么严重。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Why is there less damage this time?
sentences.zh: 为什么这次的破坏较小？

sentences.en: One of the biggest reasons is that the federal government, local governments came together and built a massive multi-billion dollar, 350 mile ring essentially around New Orleans
sentences.zh: 其中一个最大的原因，是联邦政府和地方政府联合起来，在新奥尔良周围基本上修建了一个耗资数百亿美元、长达350英里的环形防御圈，

sentences.en: of improved levees, locks, floodgates.
sentences.zh: 由改良的堤坝、船闸和防洪闸组成。

sentences.en: This was one of the most ambitious public works projects in the last few decades in this country.
sentences.zh: 这是这个国家几十年来最雄心勃勃的公共工程项目之一。

sentences.en: And it was all spurred by the outrage and the horror and the concern that people felt both
sentences.zh: 这一切的推动力，来自于人们看到2005年堤坝溃决时的景象时，

sentences.en: inside and outside of the city when they saw what happened when the levees failed in 2005.
sentences.zh: 在城内和城外感受到的愤怒、恐惧和担忧。

sentences.en: There's some asterisks here to the notion that this new system saved the city.
sentences.zh: 对于这个新系统拯救了这座城市的说法，这里还有一些需要打问号的地方。

sentences.en: For one, every hurricane is different.
sentences.zh: 首先，每场飓风都不一样。

sentences.en: This one headed to the west of the city and it was a very different track than Katrina.
sentences.zh: 这场风暴朝着城市西部袭来，它的路径与卡特里娜非常不同。

sentences.en: It also appears that the storm surge that was predicted wasn't quite as high in the end.
sentences.zh: 而且看来预测的风暴潮最终也没有那么高。

sentences.en: But I think in the end you can really say that it was indeed a success.
sentences.zh: 但我想最终你可以真正说它确实成功了。

sentences.en: And this country built something very big and very, very expensive.
sentences.zh: 这个国家建造了一些非常巨大且非常非常昂贵的东西。

sentences.en: And it kind of did its job.
sentences.zh: 它算是完成了它的工作。

sentences.en: And what does this levee system actually look like?
sentences.zh: 这个堤坝系统实际上长什么样？

sentences.en: How does it work for those of us who aren't levee experts?
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些不是堤坝专家的人来说，它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Well, I'm not a levee expert either, but I can tell you that it's many things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也不是堤坝专家，但我可以告诉你它包含很多东西。

sentences.en: In some cases, it's strengthened levees, levee walls.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它是加固的堤坝和堤防墙。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are things that you don't really always see if you're living in this very urban environment in this old city of New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，有些东西如果你住在这个新奥尔良老城的这种非常喧闹的城市环境中，你并不总是能看到。

sentences.en: But it's out there.
sentences.zh: 但它就在那里。

sentences.en: And some of this stuff is like Hoover Dam level huge.
sentences.zh: 而且其中一些东西大得像胡佛水坝级别。

sentences.en: A few years ago, I went fishing out by one of these massive new gates.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我到这些巨大的新防洪闸之一附近钓鱼。

sentences.en: It's, I mean, imagine a kind of placid wetland and then like this kind of Star Wars, Death
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想象一下某种平静的湿地，然后就像这种星战死

sentences.en: Star level, you know, concrete, you know, edifice just stuck out there.
sentences.zh: 星级别的，你知道的，混凝土结构，你知道的，就杵在那里。

sentences.en: It's really impressive.
sentences.zh: 这真的很让人震撼。

sentences.en: But it's, you know, one of the dynamics that's been interesting here is that people don't trust the government after Katrina.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这里有趣的动态之一是人们在卡特里娜之后不信任政府。

sentences.en: You know, they've been told that this thing exists.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们被告知这东西存在。

sentences.en: But like I said, it's really hard to see it.
sentences.zh: 但就像我说的，这真的很难看到。

sentences.en: And you can't really see it just all at once.
sentences.zh: 而且你不可能一下子全部看到。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to really grasp how big and how vast it is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它到底有多大、多广，很难真正领会。

sentences.en: And there was definitely an interesting tension here between people this week who are saying, oh, I don't trust this system.
sentences.zh: 本周这里的人们之间肯定存在一种有趣的紧张关系，有人说，哦，我不信任这个系统。

sentences.en: I don't care what they say or how many billions they spent versus a lot of people who really know the system who are saying, no, no, it's like, it's real.
sentences.zh: 我不管他们怎么说或者花了多少亿，而很多真正了解这个系统的人则说，不，不，这就像，它是真的。

sentences.en: Like we really spent the billions and we have some really smart engineers.
sentences.zh: 就像我们真的花了数十亿，而且我们有一些非常聪明的工程师。

sentences.en: Like it's hard to trust the government after what happened with Katrina.
sentences.zh: 经历了卡特里娜之后，很难再去信任政府。

sentences.en: And the loss of confidence in government entities after Katrina was really, really intense.
sentences.zh: 卡特里娜之后，对政府机构失去信心的情绪非常非常强烈。

sentences.en: And it certainly lingers to this day.
sentences.zh: 而且这种情绪当然一直延续到今天。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And of course, now with a couple days of reporting and hindsight, we know that Hurricane Ida did come and the levees held.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在经过几天的报道和事后回顾，我们知道飓风艾达确实来了，而堤坝顶住了。

sentences.en: And I wonder if there's a part of you that thinks that this is a story of things working.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是不是有一部分人认为这是一个事物发挥作用的故事。

sentences.en: Do you feel any sense of that on the ground with the people you're talking to?
sentences.zh: 你和当地人交谈时，有没有感受到这种情绪？

sentences.en: Because when you talk to people, it sounds like they're dealing with very real issues in their own lives.
sentences.zh: 因为当你和人们交谈时，听起来他们正在应对自己生活中非常现实的问题。

sentences.en: They're maybe not thinking about, well, I'm glad we funded that levee system.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不会想，嗯，我很高兴我们资助了那个堤坝系统。

sentences.en: Well, you know, there's very little sense of celebration here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，这里几乎没有什么庆祝的感觉。

sentences.en: And part of that has to do with the fact that as of right now, there's a humanitarian crisis looming in New Orleans, even though it's dry.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，截至目前，新奥尔良正面临着一场迫在眉睫的人道主义危机，尽管这里是干的。

sentences.en: There's no electricity.
sentences.zh: 这里没有电。

sentences.en: And with no electricity, there's no air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 没有电就没有空调。

sentences.en: And we're in late August, early September in South Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于路易斯安那州南部的八月下旬、九月初。

sentences.en: It's sweltering to the point of dangerous.
sentences.zh: 天气闷热得危险。

sentences.en: The heat index is 100 plus every day and will be for many days.
sentences.zh: 每天的热量指数都超过100华氏度，而且这种天气还将持续好几天。

sentences.en: We don't know when the energy is going to come back.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道什么时候能恢复供电。

sentences.en: People don't have jobs to go to.
sentences.zh: 人们没有工作可去。

sentences.en: The schools are closed.
sentences.zh: 学校都停课了。

sentences.en: In Jefferson Parish, which is the suburban parish right next door to Orleans Parish, nobody has any water right now.
sentences.zh: 在杰斐逊堂区，也就是紧邻奥尔良堂区的郊区堂区，现在每个人都没有水。

sentences.en: The lines for gasoline are four plus hours for those places that are open.
sentences.zh: 对于那些营业的加油站，排队加油的时间要四个多小时。

sentences.en: People are cooking their last food from the refrigerators that they've cleaned out.
sentences.zh: 人们正在用他们清理出来的冰箱里的最后一些食物做饭。

sentences.en: The people who are living in these sweltering apartments, who are infirm, who have issues with
sentences.zh: 那些住在闷热公寓里的、体弱多病的、有健康问题的人，

sentences.en: health, are potentially headed to a health care system that was already way overtaxed due to COVID-19 and the new Delta variant related spike.
sentences.zh: 可能正在走向一个由于COVID-19和新的德尔塔变异株相关激增而已经不堪重负的医疗系统。

sentences.en: From the vantage of us right now who are in the city, it doesn't feel like things are fixed.
sentences.zh: 从我们这些目前身处这座城市的人的角度来看，感觉事情并没有修好。

sentences.en: It feels like we're confronting major, major challenges.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们正在面对重大得多的挑战。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like it's hard to focus on the silver lining when the cloud is so big.
sentences.zh: 就像当乌云这么大时，很难专注于一线生机。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the silver lining only helps so much.
sentences.zh: 而一线生机也帮不了多少忙。

sentences.en: You know, I've been thinking a lot in the last day or so about the toll that even this storm, which didn't swamp the city, has taken.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，过去一天左右，我一直在想，连这场没有淹没城市的风暴也带来了这么大的代价。

sentences.en: I mean, for one, you have all these outlying areas that have been very badly hit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首先，你所有的这些外围地区都遭到重创。

sentences.en: They were hit by heavy rain.
sentences.zh: 它们遭到了暴雨袭击。

sentences.en: They were hit by wind.
sentences.zh: 它们遭到了强风袭击。

sentences.en: The city of Homa, Louisiana has been very badly beaten up.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州的霍玛市遭到了非常严重的破坏。

sentences.en: And we know from researchers that we're going to see stronger storms, most likely, and we're going to see more frequent storMs.
sentences.zh: 从研究人员那里我们知道，我们极有可能看到更强烈的风暴，而且我们会看到更频繁的风暴。

sentences.en: And I really fear now that the city is just going to continue to suffer despite the incredible resilience of the people who live here.
sentences.zh: 我现在真的很担心，尽管这里居民有着令人难以置信的韧性，这座城市仍将继续遭受苦难。

sentences.en: I mean, how can the city not continue to be diminished?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这座城市怎么能不继续衰落呢？

sentences.en: Who can afford, literally, to live through this every year?
sentences.zh: 谁能真的负担得起每年都经历这一切？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Richard, you raised the question of how many residents of New Orleans will continue to stay in the city and how long they'll stay for.
sentences.zh: 理查德，你提出了一个问题，即新奥尔良会有多少居民继续留在这座城市，他们会呆多久。

sentences.en: What did you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I grew up here and to me, this is always just like the center of the universe and most New Orleans people feel that way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我在这里长大，对我来说，这里永远就像宇宙的中心，大多数新奥尔良人都是这么觉得的。

sentences.en: But I'm really increasingly concerned about the stresses on so many of the people who have given the world this incredible culture, food, music, and just the people who are here
sentences.zh: 但我越来越担心那些给世界带来这种不可思议的文化、食物、音乐的人们所承受的压力，以及那些在这里

sentences.en: trying to live and get by and have a normal life.
sentences.zh: 努力生活、勉强度日并过上正常生活的人们。

sentences.en: There's, I think, for a very long time going to be a group of very privileged people who are going to live very well in New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在很长一段时间里，将会有一群非常特权的人在新奥尔良生活得非常好。

sentences.en: And I'm staying in uptown New Orleans right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在住在新奥尔良上城。

sentences.en: And when I went on a walk this morning to go see if the grocery store was open, you could hear the sound of privilege.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我去散步看看杂货店是否开门时，你能听到特权的声音。

sentences.en: And it sounds like, you know, kind of the low hum of a gas powered generator that's keeping the AC blowing in some of these nicer homes and is allowing people to live through this
sentences.zh: 听起来就像，你知道的，燃气发电机低沉的嗡嗡声，它让其中一些较好的家里的空调运转，让人们在冷啤酒的陪伴下度过

sentences.en: thing with cold beer and, you know, to cook gumbo and to keep a refrigerator running.
sentences.zh: 这一切，你知道的，煮秋葵汤并让冰箱保持运转。

sentences.en: And, you know, that really stands in contrast with so many of the people I talked to and so many of the people we know who have left, you know, first a middle-class person, not
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这与我交谈过的很多人以及我们认识的许多离开的人形成了鲜明的对比，你知道的，首先是一个中产阶级，

sentences.en: to mention a working class person going out and staying in a hotel for four or five days with your kids.
sentences.zh: 更不用说一个工人阶级带着孩子去外面住四五天酒店了。

sentences.en: It becomes very trying.
sentences.zh: 这变得非常煎熬。

sentences.en: And of course, for some people, it's just untenable and it can break them.
sentences.zh: 当然，对某些人来说，这简直难以维持，会把他们压垮。

sentences.en: And for the poor, they have no way to get out.
sentences.zh: 至于穷人，他们没有办法离开。

sentences.en: They're stuck in a very difficult situation without power.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入了断电的困境中。

sentences.en: I just really wonder how long people are going to be able to stand this.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想知道人们还能忍受多久。

sentences.en: If this is something that we see with more frequent and more powerful hurricanes, are they going to want to stick it out even in a city that just generates like a tremendous
sentences.zh: 如果这是我们在更频繁、更强大的飓风中看到的情况，他们还会想要坚持下去吗，即使是在一个在其居民中

sentences.en: amount of love among its inhabitants?
sentences.zh: 产生巨大热爱的城市里？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It sounds like for a lot of people in New Orleans, they don't have the money to leave.
sentences.zh: 听起来对于新奥尔良的很多人来说，他们没有钱离开。

sentences.en: Like they can't get a hotel room.
sentences.zh: 就像他们订不起酒店房间一样。

sentences.en: They can't move themselves and their families out of town for a couple of days or maybe even a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 他们无法让自己和家人离开城镇几天甚至几周。

sentences.en: And they also, in some sense, don't have the money to stay.
sentences.zh: 而且从某种意义上说，他们也没有钱留下来。

sentences.en: Like they can't get a generator.
sentences.zh: 就像他们买不起发电机一样。

sentences.en: They can't do the things that would help them maintain a basic standard of living.
sentences.zh: 他们无法做那些能帮助他们维持基本生活水平的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I remember talking to a native New Orleanian who's an old friend of mine after Katrina.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我记得在卡特里娜之后与一位我的老朋友、新奥尔良本地人交谈过。

sentences.en: And I said, well, how's the city faring?
sentences.zh: 我问，这座城市情况怎么样？

sentences.en: And he said to me, well, you know, the people who were doing all right before the storm are doing fine.
sentences.zh: 他对我说，嗯，你知道，风暴前过得不错的人现在过得很好。

sentences.en: And the people who were kind of just on the bubble of doing all right, they're not doing very well right now.
sentences.zh: 而那些处在过得不错的边缘的人，他们现在过得不是很好。

sentences.en: And then, you know, that doesn't even begin to describe what's happening to the people kind of economically below that level.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，这甚至还无法形容经济上低于这个水平的人正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: I think Warren Buffett said, you know, that when the tide goes out, you really know who's got their drawers on or not.
sentences.zh: 我想沃伦·巴菲特说过，你知道的，当潮水退去时，你才真正知道谁穿着底裤，谁没穿。

sentences.en: And, you know, you feel that after a storm like this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，经历这样一场风暴后，你会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: And what has this reality of just constantly making these choices about leaving or staying, what has that meant for the city and its population as a whole?
sentences.zh: 不断做出离开或留下这些选择的现实，对这座城市及其整体人口意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, we saw a tremendous population decline after Katrina.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在卡特里娜之后看到了巨大的人口下降。

sentences.en: And you see cultures that were transformed in Houston, Texas, to cite one important example, and Atlanta, where I live now, there are just a lot more New Orleans people there.
sentences.zh: 你会看到文化在德克萨斯州休斯顿发生了转变，仅举一个重要的例子，还有我现在居住的亚特兰大，那里有更多的新奥尔良人。

sentences.en: And one of the things that you heard that I heard one guy say to me, he was heading off to Sugar Land, Texas, which is right by Houston.
sentences.zh: 你听到的一件事情，我听到一个人对我说，他正前往德克萨斯州的舒格兰，就在休斯顿旁边。

sentences.en: You know, he's packing up his car with his kids and family and stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他正把车装满他的孩子、家人和东西。

sentences.en: I said, do you have people there?
sentences.zh: 我问，你在那里有人吗？

sentences.en: And he said, yeah, I've got family there.
sentences.zh: 他说，有，我在那里有家人。

sentences.en: They left in Katrina and they never came back.
sentences.zh: 他们在卡特里娜时离开，就再也没有回来。

sentences.en: And it was the day before the 16th anniversary of Katrina.
sentences.zh: 那天正好是卡特里娜16周年纪念日前一天。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, we're going to go have a, you know, a Sweet 16 reunion.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道的，我们要去开一个，你知道的，甜蜜16岁重聚派对。

sentences.en: The culture of New Orleans is now kind of spread out, you know, from Houston up to Atlanta and beyond.
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良的文化现在有点散落各处，你知道的，从休斯顿到亚特兰大及更远的地方。

sentences.en: And it seems like to return to Hurricane Ida a little bit, there's this kind of metaphor that is sort of sort of forming in my mind about the sort of futility of trying to engineer
sentences.zh: 而且似乎回到飓风艾达本身，我脑海中正在形成这样一种隐喻，关于试图用工程手段摆脱

sentences.en: our way out of a climate crisis.
sentences.zh: 气候危机的徒劳。

sentences.en: Because despite this fact of the levies, this multi-billion dollar infrastructure project actually working, all this human ingenuity and political will that New Orleans marshaled
sentences.zh: 因为尽管有这些防洪堤的存在，这个耗资数十亿美元的基础设施项目确实发挥了作用，新奥尔良汇聚了所有这些人类的智慧和政治意愿

sentences.en: to protect itself from another Katrina level storm, it's still not somehow equal to the task of protecting the city from a storm and making the city into a place that people can
sentences.zh: 来保护自己免受卡特里娜级别风暴的袭击，但不知为何，它仍然无法胜任保护城市免受风暴袭击的任务，也无法让这座城市成为一个人们能够

sentences.en: live in and thrive in, even if they're not wealthy.
sentences.zh: 安居乐业的地方，即使他们并不富有。

sentences.en: The amount of ingenuity and necessary hubris and vision that went into building this system around the city, to me, it just like, it smacks of like an Old Testament kind of story,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，建造这套环城系统所投入的智慧、必要的傲慢与远见，简直就像是

sentences.en: you know, like, and the people built this thing, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像是《旧约》里的那种故事，人们建造了这个东西，对吧？

sentences.en: And then the Lord was like, yeah, well, good for you.
sentences.zh: 然后上帝就像是在说，好吧，算你们厉害。

sentences.en: But guess what?
sentences.zh: 但你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: You know, that's like one-tenth of your problem solved right there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就好比你们的问题只解决十分之一。

sentences.en: There is a huge swath of the Gulf CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 墨西哥湾沿岸有一大片地区。

sentences.en: A lot of it, you know, is full of people who are just as worthy of saving as the people of New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，其中许多地方住满了和新奥尔良人民一样值得拯救的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, where's their wall?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们的防洪墙在哪里？

sentences.en: These hurricanes strike all over.
sentences.zh: 这些飓风到处袭击。

sentences.en: The sea levels are rising, you know, all up and down the Atlantic Coast and beyond.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，海平面在整个大西洋沿岸及更远的地方都在上升。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm wondering about, you mentioned there are places other than New Orleans that don't have this kind of infrastructure, these levees to protect themselves from flooding and from
sentences.zh: 我想知道的是，你提到除了新奥尔良之外，还有其他地方没有这种基础设施，没有这些防洪堤来保护自己免受洪水和

sentences.en: storMs.
sentences.zh: 风暴的侵袭。

sentences.en: How are they dealing with Hurricane Ida?
sentences.zh: 它们是如何应对飓风艾达的？

sentences.en: Well, you know, there are a lot of areas south and west, as I mentioned, that are hurting really bad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，正如我所提到的，南部和西部的许多地区受灾非常严重。

sentences.en: There's a proposed project that's kind of in the works called the Morganza to the Gulf
sentences.zh: 有一个正在筹备中的拟议项目，叫做摩根扎至墨西哥湾

sentences.en: Project.
sentences.zh: 项目。

sentences.en: It's very similar to the ring around New Orleans that would contain some of these places like
sentences.zh: 它非常类似于环绕新奥尔良的护城河系统，将把其中一些地方包括在内，比如

sentences.en: the city of Houma, Louisiana, which is this, you know, kind of oil patch city and others.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州的霍玛市，你知道的，这是一个石油重镇以及其他地方。

sentences.en: But, you know, hurricanes are complex things in themselves.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，飓风本身是复杂的。

sentences.en: And, you know, building a levee or a wall can help you prevent inundation from storm surge if you're lucky and smart.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果你幸运且明智的话，建造防洪堤或防洪墙可以帮助你防止风暴潮带来的淹没。

sentences.en: But there's also the question of wind.
sentences.zh: 但这也存在风力的问题。

sentences.en: And there's also the question of rainfall.
sentences.zh: 同时这也存在降雨的问题。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, when you look at Louisiana and much of the south, including Tennessee,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，当你审视路易斯安那州和包括田纳西州在内的许多南方地区时

sentences.en: just the other day, a lot of these flooding events we're having in this moment are coming from storms, some of them unnamed kind of like day-to-day storms that will just sit and
sentences.zh: 就在前几天，我们在此时经历的许多洪水都来自于风暴，其中一些是无名风暴，有点像日常风暴，它们会停留在

sentences.en: park themselves over a community and just trash them.
sentences.zh: 一个社区上空一动不动，然后彻底摧毁它们。

sentences.en: And, you know, those are the kinds of problems that building a wall really doesn't solve.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这些是建造防洪墙根本无法解决的问题。

sentences.en: Richard, in some sense, what you're describing, it sounds like, is a great American city, New
sentences.zh: 理查德，从某种意义上说，你所描述的听起来就像是一个伟大的美国城市——新

sentences.en: Orleans, that has become, if not uninhabitable due to climate disasters, at least a lot harder and more expensive to keep open and livable.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良，由于气候灾难，它即使没有变得不宜居，至少在维持开放和适宜居住方面也变得更加困难且成本高昂。

sentences.en: And I'm also thinking about friends of mine, privileged friends of mine, I guess, who are planning
sentences.zh: 我也在想我的朋友们，我想是一些享有特权的的朋友，他们正计划

sentences.en: to leave California for a few months this fall to get away from the fires and the smoke.
sentences.zh: 在今年秋天离开加利福尼亚几个月，以躲避火灾和烟雾。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm just meditating on the fact that in America, because of climate change, there are some people who are leaving home because they don't have any other choice.
sentences.zh: 我想我只是在思考这样一个事实：在美国，由于气候变化，有些人因为别无选择而离开家园。

sentences.en: And there are some people who are leaving home because they do.
sentences.zh: 而有些人离开家园是因为他们有得选。

sentences.en: They're privileged enough to be able to move somewhere safer.
sentences.zh: 他们享有足够的特权，能够搬到更安全的地方。

sentences.en: But both groups are leaving home.
sentences.zh: 但这两群人都在离开家园。

sentences.en: I think it's dawning on everybody that so many people in our country are having to come up with
sentences.zh: 我认为所有人都逐渐意识到，我国的许多人不得不为他们生存最基本要素制定

sentences.en: a plan B for the very most basic element of their existence, which is, you know, sort of where do I need to be because of, you know, tragedy X.
sentences.zh: B计划，也就是，你知道的，因为某种灾难X，我究竟需要在哪里。

sentences.en: It's the problem that New Orleans faces is a problem that so many communities face, sometimes in a different guise, you know, with a different challenge.
sentences.zh: 新奥尔良面临的问题是许多社区都面临的问题，有时只是换了件外衣，你知道的，面临着不同的挑战。

sentences.en: But it's become a universal fact of life for people all over the place.
sentences.zh: 但它已经成为各地人们生活中普遍存在的事实。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I know that, Richard, you're there in New Orleans reporting on this in your professional capacity.
sentences.zh: 我知道，理查德，你就在新奥尔良，以你的专业身份报道这件事。

sentences.en: But as someone who still has family there and who has spent a lot of time in New Orleans,
sentences.zh: 但作为F一个在那里仍有家人并且在新奥尔良度过了很多时间的人

sentences.en: I'm wondering how you and your family are thinking about your own version of these questions, whether New Orleans is still the right place to be,
sentences.zh: 我想知道你和你的家人是如何看待你们自己对这些问题的看法的，新奥尔良是否仍然是一个合适的地方

sentences.en: what New Orleans will even be 10 or 20 years from now.
sentences.zh: 从现在起10年或20年后的新奥尔良甚至会变成什么样。

sentences.en: You know, these kinds of processes happen over such a long timeline sometimes in this era of climate crisis.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在这个气候危机时代，这类过程有时会在如此漫长的时间线内发生。

sentences.en: You know, the way that I think a lot of people, myself included, sort of thought about how a tragedy that would befall a city would happen are not quite accurate.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为很多人（包括我自己）曾经想象灾难降临城市的方式其实并不准确。

sentences.en: It's not the Godzilla, you know, who comes and destroys the city in five minutes breathing fire.
sentences.zh: 它不是哥斯拉，你知道的，喷着火在五分钟内摧毁城市。

sentences.en: And maybe it's not even Katrina, you know, where, you know, one day you're dry, the next day you're 80% underwater and there's more than a thousand people dead.
sentences.zh: 也许它甚至不是卡特里娜飓风，你知道的，前一天你还干爽，第二天有80%的面积在水下，有超过一千人死亡。

sentences.en: You know, this longer term tragedy that unfolds is the thing that I'm really concerned about, which is, and I think concerns everyone, which is that, you know, over decades,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这种长期展开的悲剧才是我真正关心的事，这也是我认为每个人都关心的事，那就是，你知道的，几十年来

sentences.en: there's just a tremendous weakening of a place and it's almost impossible to stop.
sentences.zh: 一个地方正在经历极大的衰落，而且几乎无法阻止。

sentences.en: Richard, stay safe, stay dry, stay cool to the extent possible, and thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 理查德，请保重安全，保持干爽，在可能的情况下保持凉爽，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，凯文。

sentences.en: As of Wednesday night, the death toll from Hurricane Ida and its aftermath rose to at least eight.
sentences.zh: 截至周三晚间，飓风艾达及其余波造成的死亡人数已上升至至少8人。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Louisiana's largest utility, Entergy, said it had restored power to more than 11,000 customers in New Orleans.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，路易斯安那州最大的公用事业公司安特吉（Entergy）表示，它已为新奥尔良超过11,000名用户恢复了电力。

sentences.en: But more than a million customers across the state of Louisiana were still without power.
sentences.zh: 但路易斯安那州全境仍有超过一百万用户处于断电状态。

sentences.en: And the company says it could take weeks or even months to fully restore power across the state.
sentences.zh: 该公司表示，可能需要数周甚至数月才能完全恢复全州的电力供应。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the nation's most restrictive abortion law went into effect in Texas after the Supreme Court did not act on a request to stop it.
sentences.zh: 周三，在最高法院未对阻止该法的请求采取行动后，美国限制性最强的堕胎法在得克萨斯州生效。

sentences.en: The law blocks most abortions after just six weeks of pregnancy, before many women even know they're pregnant, and therefore amounts to an almost total ban on abortion.
sentences.zh: 该法律在怀孕仅六周后就禁止了大多数堕胎，此时许多女性甚至还不知道自己怀孕，因此这几乎等同于全面禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: In the hours after the law went into effect, abortion providers across Texas began turning away women seeking the procedure.
sentences.zh: 在该法律生效后的几小时内，得克萨斯州各地的堕胎服务提供者开始拒绝寻求该手术的女性。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了许多自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争中。
